note: Events marked captured:true are raw socket2 lines recorded on Omarchy 4.0.2 / Hyprland 0.56.2 via `socat -U - UNIX-CONNECT:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket2.sock`. They confirm OWNER arrives as the std::formatter spelling, not an integer. Window and region rows are synthetic: capturing them needs a portal client driven by hand, and the parse they exercise is the same one the captured monitor rows prove. The integer-OWNER rows are deliberately synthetic -- they guard a hypothetical build without the std::formatter<eScreenshareType> specialization, which this one has.
observations: screencast (v1) is always posted immediately BEFORE screencastv2 for the same session, so seeing v1 is not evidence that v2 is missing.

grim holds a monitor session open for ~500 ms and is torn down by Hyprland's idle-stop timer, not by an immediate client disconnect. Measured 06.108 -> 06.608 and 11.130 -> 11.630. A debounce at or below 500 ms would flash a ring on every screenshot; the 700 ms default swallows it.
grim with no -o argument opens one session per output: three concurrent sessions on a three-output setup, each with its own start and stop.

events.why: grim -o DP-1: monitor share start. OWNER is the string, not 0
grim -o DP-1: matching stop 500 ms later
grim across all outputs: second concurrent session
grim across all outputs: third concurrent session
matching stop for the window share
NAME contains commas; must not be truncated
region share; NAME is the monitor connector, no box on the wire
empty NAME must not be guessed at
SHARE_NONE formats as "ERR NONE" and is not a target
